name: Sri Kakatiya Rudreshwara (Ramappa) Swamy Temple
address: Palampet Village, Venkatapur Mandal, Mulugu District, Telangana - 506345
description: The Ramappa Temple, also known as the Kakatiya Rudreshwara Temple, is a 13th-century engineering marvel and a UNESCO World Heritage Site (inscribed in July 2021 as India's 39th World Heritage Site). It stands as a glorious testament to the royal patronage, architectural brilliance, and artistic craftsmanship of the Kakatiya Dynasty.
history: Built in 1213 CE by Racherla Rudra, a general under the Kakatiya ruler King Ganapati Deva. Popularly named after its master sculptor or architect, Ramappa, making it one of the rare Indian temples named after its artisan rather than its presiding deity. Declared a UNESCO World Heritage Site in July 2021.
mythology: Features 13th-century Kakatiya architecture incorporating floating bricks technology (roof shikhara constructed using lightweight porous bricks that float on water) and sandbox foundation technique for earthquake resistance. Dolerite/basalt stone pillars feature mirror-polished carved dancer (Madanika) figures.
sub_temples: Nandi Mandapam (Housing the monolithic Nandi statue)
